gate_4_source_validation.metric: validation_macro_log_q95 at step 4000, re-scored at a fixed inner_steps
gate_4_source_validation.protocol_correction: The baseline checkpoints were validated with inner_steps=0 (zero-shot); the struct config used inner_steps=5. validate() reads config['inner_steps'], so the previously published table paired a zero-shot baseline with a 5-step-adapted struct arm. All six checkpoints were re-scored at both settings with scripts/validate_inner_steps.py; the raw output is step6_inner_steps_protocol.json.
gate_4_source_validation.verdict: The gate's verdict depends on the reading. (i) Selected checkpoint scored under the baseline's own protocol (inner_steps=0): +12.88/+44.42/+17.63%, FAILS. (ii) Selected checkpoint scored under the struct config's protocol (inner_steps=5): -1.30/-4.30/+4.22%, passes; that protocol favours the struct arm, because 5-step adaptation worsens the baseline by 1.5-5.0% but improves the struct arm by 8.2-31.2%. (iii) Each run's own best_metric: +1.31/-1.56/+3.43%, passes, but the two sides are then measured under different protocols at different steps and neither is the checkpoint used downstream. The only reading that is both protocol-matched and at the operating point used by the K=0 target evaluation (zero-shot) is (i), which fails.

selection_reading.note: A third reading compares each run's own best_metric (the source-validation selection value stored in the checkpoint). Each side then uses its own protocol (baseline inner_steps=0, struct inner_steps=5) and its own best step, so this is not a matched-protocol comparison either, but doc 118 section 2.2 says 'source-validation selection' and this is the literal selection value.

stop_condition_2_bare_anchor.rule: doc 118 section 6.2: if the trained model is worse than the closed-form anchor on source validation, drop the correction head
stop_condition_2_bare_anchor.measurement: A fresh SetEstimator(width=64, use_pg=False, arch=sum, layers=2, heads=4, anchor=struct) has a zero-initialised last layer; torch.manual_seed(0); the same 75-episode source validation plan; log at step6_bare_anchor_protocols.log.
stop_condition_2_bare_anchor.counterexample: At inner_steps=0 (the anchor's own protocol, deterministic) seed 43 scores 3.8801 vs the bare anchor's 3.6722, i.e. 5.66% worse; seeds 42/44 improve. At inner_steps=5 all three seeds improve (-21% to -26%). The head helps on average, not always.

superseded_value.why: Produced by a fresh model whose random seed was not recorded, at inner_steps=5; a 5-step score depends on the random weights under the zero-initialised layer, so it is not the pure-anchor value. Superseded by the inner_steps=0 measurement 3.6722.

stop_condition_2_bare_anchor.literal_reference_not_measured: Doc 118 section 6.2 names C_uncond; C_uncond was measured in doc 119 on a different 600-query (4-7 table) set and is not available on this 75-episode source validation plan. The bare struct anchor on the same plan is the substitute used here, so the literal stop condition was not evaluated.
stop_condition_2_bare_anchor.verdict: Not triggered under either measured protocol, but not clean: at inner_steps=0 seed 43 scores 3.8801 vs the bare anchor's 3.6722 (+5.66%, worse), while seeds 42/44 improve; at inner_steps=5 all three seeds improve (-21% to -27%). The plan gives no aggregation rule across seeds or protocols, so 'the head helps on average' is the most that is supported.

target_k0.old_sum_source: 实验文档/results/p2-2-target-3seed-20261023/summary.json (same script, same maxima, same cache content hashes)

diagnosis.finding: The bare anchor's error grows with table count on all four targets when measured by the median; the q95 rise is not strictly monotone (genome 5->6 tables 9.779->9.770, ergastf1 6->7 tables 3.207->3.140). The curve mixes the structural-independence error with the 160-bin approximation, which doc 119 section 3 measured on a different query set (4 tables: binned 8.81 vs exact 9.558, within that section's bootstrap noise; 5 tables 12.24 vs 7.399; 6 tables 41.24 vs 15.967; 7 tables 6.03 vs 3.055). Two-table medians are 0.227-0.586, so the sidecar/queries path is not broken; the script's intended n=1 control is unavailable because no target database has 1-table queries.
diagnosis.head_effect: The head lowers the anchor's q95 log error on all three seeds for imdb, stats and genome, but on ergastf1 only seed 44 improves (2.542->2.285); seeds 42 (5.388) and 43 (2.708) are worse than the bare anchor. The residual is mostly a near-uniform upward shift learned on source databases, not a fix of the target tail.
diagnosis.anchor_by_table_count_caveat: struct_log is a 160-bin approximation, and doc 119 section 3 measured that approximation degrading with table count on the same source queries (5 tables: 160-bin Q95 12.24 vs exact 7.399; 6 tables: 41.24 vs 15.967). The by-table-count curve therefore mixes the structural-independence error with the bucketing error; it does not attribute the growth to the structural estimator alone. The script's intended n=1 control is unavailable: no target database has 1-table queries (the 1-table bucket is empty in every seed summary).

stop_conditions.rule_6_2_drop_head: not triggered under either measured protocol, with one counterexample: at the anchor's own 0-step protocol seeds 42/44 beat the bare anchor but seed 43 is 5.66% worse (3.8801 vs 3.6722); at 5 steps all three seeds improve. The plan's literal reference (C_uncond on this plan) was not measured; a bare struct anchor was used as the proxy.
stop_conditions.rule_6_3_all_seeds_lose_to_pg: not triggered literally: all three seeds beat PG on imdb and genome; all three lose to PG on stats; two of three beat PG on ergastf1
stop_conditions.substantive_result: The struct anchor without PG loses to the existing PG-anchored sum baseline on three of four targets at the 3-seed mean (stats 376.4 vs 81.1, genome 976.1 vs 192.0, ergastf1 81.2 vs 23.4) and is slightly worse on imdb (36.0 vs 33.1); on the 4+ table bucket it is much better on imdb (68.2 vs 440.5) and worse on stats and genome.

reproduced_history.note: Baseline values are the history.json step-4000 rows; struct values are the same rows, reproduced by re-scoring the checkpoints at inner_steps=5 within 2.1e-07.
